findings.failure_scenario: A bid request where the user-id module populated `userIdAsEids` (e.g. [{source: 'adserver.org', uids: [{id: 'sample-userid'}]}]) but left `userId` empty/absent: the outer `if (bidRequests[0].userId)` at line 355 skips the entire block, `payload.eids` is never set, and valid user-id signals (including the TDID/UID2 partner mapping) are omitted from the AppNexus request. The changed code fixes the opposite mismatch (userId set, userIdAsEids undefined) but leaves this one: the guard belongs on `userIdAsEids`, the data actually consumed.
findings.summary: The eids block is still keyed on `bidRequests[0].userId` even though it only consumes `bidRequests[0].userIdAsEids`, so the symmetric mismatch (userIdAsEids present, userId absent) silently drops all eids — the fix guards the consumed field instead of keying on it.

findings.failure_scenario: The only eids test (test/spec/modules/appnexusBidAdapter_spec.js:1606 'should populate eids when supported userIds are available') sets `userId` and `userIdAsEids` together, so the crash path this change fixes has zero coverage: a future refactor that removes or weakens the guard reintroduces the `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'forEach')` crash with no CI signal.
findings.summary: The new `if (bidRequests[0].userIdAsEids)` guard — the entire purpose of this change (preventing a TypeError when userId is set but userIdAsEids is undefined) — is added without any regression test covering that path.

findings.failure_scenario: Non-behavioral maintainability cost: the equivalent inline form `(bidRequests[0].userIdAsEids || []).forEach(eid => {...})` provides the same undefined-guard in one line, avoiding the extra nesting and the `uids`/`eid.uids` name collision that misleads future maintainers into thinking the helper processes uids rather than eids.
findings.summary: The change wraps the unchanged loop body in a named closure `processEids(uids)` solely to attach a truthiness guard, adding an indirection layer with a misleading parameter name (the parameter receives the eids array, while the actual uids live at `eid.uids`).
